💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US Commerce Department has put Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud organization at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, on its trade blacklist, after officials and lawmakers spent weeks asking why it was taking so long.
  • Moreover, the Entity List filing also caught six firms seen as Megaspeed affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.
  • I’ve led the push for the Department of Commerce to crack down on Megaspeed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US Commerce Department has put Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud organization at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, on its trade blacklist, after officials and lawmakers spent weeks asking why it was taking so long.

Moreover, the Entity List filing also caught six firms seen as Megaspeed affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

I’ve led the push for the Department of Commerce to crack down on Megaspeed. I’m glad it’s finally moving forward.

In a recent development, the Department of Commerce still needs to explain to Congress why this took so long. Other agencies including the Departments of State, Treasury, and War supported the designation.

— Senator Pete Ricketts (@SenatorRicketts) November 23, 2026.

A place on the list means US firms need a licence to sell it goods, software, or tech, and such requests are usually refused. Listed firms also struggle to get spare parts and updates for gear they already run.

Industry observers note that US investigators have spent more than a year looking into whether Megaspeed, long one of Nvidia’s bigger customers, funnelled advanced chips into China, where export rules bar their sale. The Justice Department has opened a criminal inquiry, and Nvidia says it chose to stop selling to the firm in June 2025.

In a recent development, why the listing took so long had become a sore point at the top of the US government. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about it at a White House meeting this month, Axios reported, though Commerce indicates that never happened.

Four departments had wanted Megaspeed listed for months, but “commerce has the pen,” Bessent told CNBC this month.

According to recent reports, the scandal runs through the company’s former boss, Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang. US spy agencies reportedly came to suspect her of working for Chinese intelligence, a claim that was not confirmed until now.

Nvidia investigates after CEO admits affair linked to spy reports.

Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 11 November, after 33 years running the tech giant he co-founded. On the same day Megaspeed was blacklisted, Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to reinstate him.

Megaspeed denies doing anything wrong and says Alice Huang left the company in August 2025. The rule took effect on Monday, when it was filed for public inspection, and formal publication in the Federal Register follows on Wednesday.

Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
  • In a recent development, after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
  • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a newly introduced Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber indicates that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

In a recent development, after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Industry observers note that starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

Uber claims the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

Industry observers note that uber notes it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

In a recent development, uber claims it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, filled with photos and memes reflecting the game's satirical rendition of the U.S.
  • As such, GTA 6 players have discovered that Snapmatic can be used to identify robbery targets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) has been out for less than a week, but players have already found a plethora of considered details in the massive sandbox game. Among them is a novel method players are using to get more money in GTA 6, helping them find robbery targets that are worth their time. It also doubles as an important reminder about internet safety.

Snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, filled with photos and memes reflecting the game's satirical rendition of the U.S. This includes people showing off drugs, cars, and weapons in a bid for clout. Like Instagram, Snapmatic also allows its fictional consumers to tag a location in their posts.

As such, GTA 6 players have discovered that Snapmatic can be used to identify robbery targets. Simply find a post with a location tagged, and open the menu you'd use to like it or view comments. Under the "Like" option will be "Set Destination," which will mark the location of the Snapmatic post on your map. You can then head there to relieve characters of their belongings (typically via the use of notable violence).

Sources indicate that it's an interesting gameplay mechanic that also serves as a reminder to be careful about what you post online. While the world of GTA 6 is a heightened version of reality, it does still have some basis in truth. There have been multiple real-life instances of criminals finding their victims via social media posts, something that's been occurring for years.

It has been revealed that last month, a UK man was convicted of stealing £48,000 (about $62,900) and various items from a home after seeing the family's social media posts indicating they'd be out hosting a Chinese Latest Year celebration. In 2021, four people were arrested in Italy for allegedly stealing from celebrities and influencers after monitoring their Instagram accounts, reportedly using victims' posts to identify tagged locations, entry points, and when they'd be away from home. Back in 2016, a California man was convicted of stealing personal items from female college students after finding them via GPS locations in photos posted to Instagram.

Even if you exclude location tags and don't mention your movements in your posts, you can still be vulnerable. Late last year, four French men travelled to Australia in order to rob a home of items reportedly valued at around $AU10 million ($6.6 million). According to court documents, the thieves saw photos of luxury goods that a victim had posted to Instagram, as well as images of their backyard and local surroundings. The thieves then used ChatGPT to search for where these pictures were taken, narrowing it down to a specific Australian city and suburb, which helped them locate the house.

Industry observers note that using social media to pick robbery targets in GTA 6 won't attract the same legal consequences and prison time that it would in real life. Rather, it serves as a neat little trick to help ambitious, self-starting criminals find worthwhile heists. However, this mechanic should also serve as an key reminder about the dangers of real-life Insta-bragging, and a warning to be careful about what you share online. It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) offers a satirical rendition of the U.S., filled with cars, crime, and shenanigans worthy of the game's Florida-inspired setting. It also incorporates many digital elements of modern life, including social media. Of course, where there's social media, there are inevitably memes.

In-game social media app Snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, offering a scrollable feed of posts from fictional characters showing off their very lootable possessions. However, Snapmatic isn't just filled with posts sharing potential theft coordinates. It also contains a plethora of memes specifically created to populate GTA 6's social media.

Players quickly took note of GTA 6's memes, praising them for accurately capturing the irreverent vibe and frequently off-colour humour that typically characterises such media.

"GTA 6 is so realistic that I thought this was a real meme," posted X user @thisdopenose, sharing an image of an in-game meme. In the meme, the text "bisexuals when they realise you can have sex more than twice" is edited onto a monochrome image of a man crying. The popular post has 94,000 likes at time of writing.

"They need to give a pay rise to whoever came up with the shitposts on Snapmatic bro these things are so funny," wrote @vandalfeet.

Some of GTA 6's in-game memes even referred to memes about GTA 6 itself. It's been 13 years since GTA 5 released, with many fans having eagerly awaited the franchises' latest instalment for over a decade. In the interim, it became a common meme for people to jokingly express disbelief that various other events had occurred "before GTA 6" arrived.

Developer Rockstar Games appears to have been aware of such memes, creating its own versions referring to GTA 6's fictional video game Race and Chase 7. ("Race'n'Chase" was the original working title for the first Grand Theft Auto game released in 1997).

Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games had teams dedicated to creating in-game media, aiming to flesh out GTA 6's world and make it feel more immersive. Judging by fans' reactions, it appears to have paid off. Parent firm Take-Two Interactive estimates that GTA 6 achieved $3.79 billion in sales on day one alone, making it one of the biggest entertainment media rolls out ever. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's a commonly asked question about everyone's favorite spicy hookup site, AdultFriendFinder: Is AFF safe to use? We get it. It's nerve-wracking when things get very NSFW. Unlike other well-known dating sites, the AFF interface is full of adult content. To the untrained eye, AFF looks like a hotbed of would-be scammers. It's perfectly reasonable to question its legitimacy. AFF consumers want some fun, but they also want to be safe.

To better understand the risks of using AdultFriendFinder, we consulted Anna Larkina, a Web Data and Privacy Analysis Expert at Kaspersky, one of the world's leading cybersecurity services, to ask about the kinds of threats owners might face on AFF and how they can mitigate those risks.

To begin, it's worth remembering that there's a risk inherent to using any online service, whether it's an adult dating site or otherwise. Even the most reputable websites have been exploited and experienced major hacks over the years. “Users should remember that any service can potentially encounter various cybersecurity concerns,” Larkina told us. That includes “data leaks, attacks on third-party contractors, or issues related to the human factor.”  The best hookup apps, reviewed by our experts AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections Tinder — top pick for fast hookups Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups Pure — best for anonymous hookups OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections.

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups.

Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups.

Pure — best for anonymous hookups.

OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

Sources indicate that but the risks are, of course, higher on certain websites. With a regular merchant website, for instance, you’re only handing over your credit card information (which is very valuable, admittedly), but with a dating site, you’re potentially providing your credit card details plus crucial personal information, from your date of birth and nationality to your address and phone number. That kind of information can heighten the risk — it's very valuable to online scammers who seek to steal it for use or resale.

While this is a risk you take with literally any dating service, AdultFriendFinder is perhaps more vulnerable than most dating sites because of the nature of its content and user base. It’s vital to understand any potential security problems.

While NSFW content is permitted on AFF — it's actually encouraged — consumers are under no obligation to post nude photos of themselves, or get down and dirty on a webcam feed. Many users opt to do so, of course, and while there's no judgment here — let that freak flag fly high and proud, we say — you do risk potentially awkward conversations with family, friends, or co-workers if they happen to stumble across your account. (That would mean they'd have to fess up to being AFF users too, but even so...).

Unfortunately, bad actors can exploit and use your own personal information against you.

“Data from services with adult content or dating services can be especially sensitive for users, because it’s more personal,” warns Larkina. “If fraudsters somehow obtain such private data, they can use it for more ‘efficient’ blackmailing or targeted phishing.” Needless to say, you should be wary of how you use the site and what information you share, especially if you have a public-facing job.

While dating sites now invest heavily in cybersecurity protections, online threats are constant and keep evolving. Hackers eager to discover treasure troves of personal and financial information often target online dating platforms, which can make owners feel super vulnerable.

Recent findings suggest that adultFriendFinder has suffered two major security breaches, which is actually a pretty stellar record of security over its entire 30-year history. In 2016, hackers gained access to the personal information of four million AFF customers before the breach was found and stopped. And a larger breach occurred in 2016, affecting some 300 million AFF accounts, including 15 million that had been officially deleted by users but whose data had not been properly expunged from the AFF servers.

It has been revealed that to combat phishing, AFF offers the option to verify your identity with government-issued identification. This verification process is still optional — it's not required when setting up an account. We recommend doing it and setting a search filter to verified accounts only. That way you'll only interact with people who are 100% legit. It's a surefire way to protect yourself against scammers.

While the private information you give AFF (your real name and email address, for example) isn't public-facing, AFF’s dating profiles are public by default, so if you include a picture of your face (as many accounts do), you can be recognized by friends, co-workers, and family members.

And since AFF has suffered two major hacks before, there’s always a chance it could happen again, which could result in your email address and information ending up in a dodgy database.

Sources indicate that does this all mean you should never use AdultFriendFinder, or any dating site? Absolutely not. We're here to help you protect yourself and stay vigilant, not to discourage you from signing up.

Larkina has shared an additional list of best practices to help you mitigate risks while having fun on AFF or any other dating site:.

To protect your accounts, use strong and unique passwords, change them regularly, and if possible, enable two-factor authentication.

Recent findings suggest that be extremely cautious with what you share with strangers, especially when it comes to sensitive information or intimate photos. “Always assess reputational and other risks before posting or sending anything,” cautions Larkina.

When using AFF in particular, limit your interactions to people who have verified their identity.

Summing up her advice, Larkina urges online dating service consumers to treat these “platforms as public spaces, not as private ones” as far as possible, and be ever mindful that “every piece of data you provide — email, phone number, username, etc. — becomes part of your digital footprint.” If you’re careful about what you share and who you share it with, you can safely enjoy AdultFriendFinder and any other dating site.

  • There was no online component at launch, nor has Rockstar confirmed any intention of adding one after launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI was released on consoles last week, with millions of players exploring Leonida on Xbox and PS5 consoles. But one major question remains: What's happening with the online mode?

According to recent reports, the GTA Online component of Grand Theft Auto V has kept that 13-year-old game relevant across three console generations, with a recent leak suggesting Rockstar makes as much as $500 million annually from microtransactions alone. One would think that means GTA VI will have a similar online offering available at launch, but that isn't the case. Per a Rockstar statement given to IGN, as well as all available marketing language on digital storefronts, GTA VI is a "single-player experience.".

There was no online component at launch, nor has Rockstar confirmed any intention of adding one after launch. Sadly, that is all the concrete information anyone can provide right now.

However, that doesn't mean all hope is lost. It's worth remembering that both GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 rolled out as solo experiences and got online modes later, though it was only a matter of months in both cases. Given that Rockstar hasn't even stated if there will be a new GTA Online experience for VI, it's probably safe to assume the wait will be longer this time.

In a recent development, the fact that the existing GTA Online is so wildly successful (with no signs of slowing down) means Rockstar isn't necessarily incentivized to make a newly introduced one right away. It also means Rockstar has to decide if it wants to keep two different GTA Online experiences running at the same time, should GTA VI ever get one. As IGN noted, Grand Theft Auto publisher Take-Two currently supports two different NBA 2K Online games in the Asian market; the first launched in 2012 and its sequel in 2017, but they're both popular enough to coexist to this day.

Unfortunately, we don't have a definitive answer on when we'll get a new GTA Online mode tied to the new game, but hey, single-player games aren't so bad. I'm sure there will be plenty of hours of entertainment to be had in GTA VI as it is.

GTA 6 on PC update: What we know about when it releases

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming, with limits).
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date.
  • An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming, with limits).

It has been revealed that GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date. Given Rockstar's history with PC ports, we originally thought gamers were in for a long wait.

An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI arrived on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Nov. 19, 2026, but PC players will have to wait a while longer. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will not be available for PC gamers at launch, and no PC version has been officially confirmed yet.

Sources indicate that despite that, we recently got some good news: GamesBeat reports that GTA 6 will get a PC release sometime in Q1 of 2027. GamesBeat has a good track record with unannounced news like this. According to their reporting, the GTA 6 PC release window was confirmed by industry sources familiar with Rockstar's intends. They spoke with the outlet under the condition of anonymity.

Rockstar and Take-Two haven't given an official reason for skipping PC at launch, but a few factors are typically cited when publishers stagger releases this way.

Industry observers note that console hardware is standardized, which tends to make optimization more straightforward than building for the huge range of PC configurations. Some industry data has also indicated that consoles generate higher per-unit revenue, giving publishers an incentive to front-load console sales.

According to recent reports, A more cynical take is that Take-Two could just be double-dipping, hoping fans who can't wait for the PC launch will buy the console first, then buy the PC version later. A PC Gamer poll found that 39 percent of respondents said they're fine waiting for a port rather than needing it on day one, suggesting a meaningful share of the PC audience isn't treating the delay as a dealbreaker.

However, there could be another, less financially motivated reason for all of this.

Speaking to YouTuber KiwiTalkz, former Rockstar producer John Ricchio explained that building for consoles first and scaling up to PC is technically easier than the reverse, since consoles have fixed, predictable hardware. According to IGN, Ricchio said it's simpler to start with tighter constraints and add polish later than to build a PC-first game and then try to trim it down to fit console limitations.

Without an official release date, gamers have had to speculate on the most likely launch window for a GTA 6 PC version.

If you look at several past Rockstar games, you can see that there's typically a significant amount of time between the console launch and the PC port.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 4 was released in April 2008 and didn't reach PC's until December. Grand Theft Auto V was released in Sept. 2013, and its PC counterpart was released 19 months later in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived on PC roughly a year after its console release.

The one exception was Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition, which rolled out simultaneously across platforms in 2021. Based on that track record, a GTA 6 PC port, if it follows the usual pattern, could be a year or more away.

In a recent development, A report from The Verge claimed that Xbox would have exclusive rights to stream GTA 6 via its cloud gaming service at launch, a claim that was recently confirmed. The report noted that PC gamers would be able to play GTA 6 on day one, despite Rockstar's lack of news about a potential release window for a PC port. Unfortunately, Xbox Gaming's Chief Strategy Officer, Matthew Ball, shot down this report. Ball wrote on his personal X account that The Verge's coverage led to some "misreporting.".

Again, the game will be available to play on Xbox consoles via Xbox Cloud Gaming, but that service faces strict monthly limits, which will make it difficult to play through the game in a timely fashion.

Fortunately, a GamesBeat report suggests gamers may not have to wait a full year for a PC release, though it remains unconfirmed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI has been out for less than a week, but there are already a whole host of tips, tricks and memes out there.

Recent findings suggest that rumors, too. One that we've seen repeated and reshared recently is a rumor about GTA 6's online multiplayer version, and the criteria players will supposedly need to meet in order to play it.

Industry observers note that "Rockstar Games has reportedly confirmed that players will be required to achieve 100% single-player story completion—including all stranger missions and collectibles—before being granted access to 'GTA 6 Online' servers at launch," posted Chaos Crave on X. At the time of writing that's had around 1,400 shares, and we've seen the claim being repeated by other accounts.

In a recent development, the problem? It's not true. As the Community Note attached to the post points out, Chaos Crave (per its own bio) is a "Satirical News account".

Rockstar Games has confirmed no such thing — and in fact, we don't even know when an online GTA 6 will be available, let alone any other details.

Will an online mode for GTA 6 be coming at some point? Probably, given how much money it makes for Rockstar. But for now, we'll just have to keep exploring the single player world.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In an open letter to the CEOs of Amazon and eBay, a coalition of 155 child advocacy groups called on the online marketplaces to stop selling toys powered by artificial intelligence.
  • The letter argues that AI toys are "cheap, easy to buy, and largely untested." It lists numerous risks associated with the products, including sexually explicit content, unproven educational claims, privacy violations, and instructions for how to access and use harmful household items.
  • The letter's publication follows the release of annual toy research conducted by U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In an open letter to the CEOs of Amazon and eBay, a coalition of 155 child advocacy groups called on the online marketplaces to stop selling toys powered by artificial intelligence.

The letter argues that AI toys are "cheap, easy to buy, and largely untested." It lists numerous risks associated with the products, including sexually explicit content, unproven educational claims, privacy violations, and instructions for how to access and use harmful household items.

The letter's publication follows the release of annual toy research conducted by U.S. PIRG. While some AI products made key safety gains compared to last year, others still have inappropriate conversations and pose considerable privacy risks.

The Alilo Smart AI Bunny, for example, told a tester where to search in their house for bleach, defined the word "fetish," discussed specific sexual scenarios, explained why lubricant can be helpful, and suggested using "padded cuffs, soft floggers, or feather ticklers.".

It has been revealed that amazon subsequently removed the bunny and another toy capable of sexual exchanges from its platform. The letter identified over 50 AI toys available for sale on Amazon's U.S. marketplace.

"These products should be shown to be safe before they reach children, not withdrawn one at a time after harm is found," the letter said.

According to recent reports, the effort was led by the child advocacy groups Fairplay, Alliance 4 Children CIC, and Set@16. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

In a recent development, on Friday, Amazon told U.S. PIRG that it had removed toys as it investigated the alleged concerns.

Recent findings suggest that "Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families," the firm stated in a statement to PIRG. "We're working with our partners across the industry and government to ensure proper guardrails for these products are in place as this technology develops.".

eBay responded to the open letter in response to Mashable's request for comment.

"We are committed to protecting the buyers and sellers on our marketplace and we continually evaluate our policies and engage with regulators to ensure our marketplace remains safe, trusted, and responsive to evolving safety standards," an eBay spokesperson remarked in an email.

Amazon told Mashable that it requires all products sold by third-parties to comply with applicable laws and regulations.

Industry observers note that "Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families," the manufacturer mentioned in an email. "We support efforts across the industry and government to put appropriate guardrails in place as this technology develops.".

The letter notes that California banned toys with companion chatbots for children younger than 16, beginning Jan. 2027. A bill introduced in Congress would also ban AI chatbots in toys.

Recent findings suggest that "You do not need to wait," the letter remarked, addressing Amazon and eBay. "Marketplaces are responsible for the safety of what they sell, and you already remove unsafe products.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Previously, the companion app still used a tall Material 3 bottom bar.
  • The tabs remain Home, Blueprint, Billing, Shop, and Support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Fi Wireless is the latest first-party app to adopt a floating toolbar as part of a small navigation redesign.

Previously, the companion app still used a tall Material 3 bottom bar. With the network switching upgrade unveiled last week, Google Fi now has a floating navigation toolbar.

The tabs remain Home, Blueprint, Billing, Shop, and Support. A pill-shaped tab indicator is leveraged, while there’s a prominent shadow effect. Given the floating nature, you see what’s around the toolbar, while Fi Wireless now extends underneath the system navigation bar.

However, the Shop tab loads a webpage as before, resulting in a gap and wasted space.

There’s now a floating action button for the newly introduced Google AI-powered Ask Fi chatbot. It provides “instant account help and troubleshooting.” If you ask for human support, the contents of the conversation carry over.

Industry observers note that this redesign is rolling out with version 171 of the app as a server-side patch. Google Fi joins Google Photos, Chat, and Pixel Now Playing in adopting floating navigation, which is likely the new first-party mandate for a more edge-to-edge design.

Industry observers note that secondary network switching is not yet widely available, with Google telling us last week that it’s a gradual rollout. The MVNO is also ending Pixel exclusivity for Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ with availability on “select” Samsung and Motorola phones.

It has been revealed that twelve South, the company behind a range of premium Apple accessories, has launched a notable expansion of its Airfly brand. The company today unveiled Airfly Drive, a dongle that turns wired CarPlay into wireless CarPlay. It’s available to order starting now. Here’s how it works.

Airfly Drive works with most cars that have factory-wired CarPlay, according to Twelve South. This covers more than 75 makes and model years back to 2014. Airfly Drive itself has a USB-A connector, but Twelve South includes a USB-C adapter in the box. It has a compact, aluminum design and is meant to stay plugged in.

Twelve South’s Airfly Drive doesn’t require an app or account. You simply plug it into your car’s USB port, pair it to your phone once, and you’re set. Going forward, the Airfly Drive will automatically reconnect to your phone to enable the wireless CarPlay experience. It also supports two paired phones, controlled by a single button that switches between them.

Twelve South outlines some specs and features:.

Wireless CarPlay is significantly more seamless than wired CarPlay, especially for those shorter trips around town. It’s a great quality-of-life upgrade for your CarPlay experience.

You can order Airfly Drive from Twelve South today for $39.99. It’s available in black and white. It also works with Android Auto.

Motorola’s Razr Flex has leaked in full, with the iPhone Duo competitor showing off its wide form factor in two colors, and it looks great.

Following a leaker earlier this morning, SammyGuru has published new images of the Razr Flex, an iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8 competitor that Motorola has been teasing for months now.

These images show the “Dark Botanical Garden” green and “Coriander” brown with woven and leather-like backplates, two rear-facing cameras, and selfie cameras on both displays. The outer display, said to be 4.97 inches, is wide but very compact, while the inner display is wide in the same way that the iPhone Duo is. The inner panel is expected to be around 7 inches in size.

SammyGuru mentions that the hinge can hold itself half-open and that the price might come in at around $1,799 – though any guesses here are up in the air in the age of RAMageddon.

Motorola Razr Flex is expected to launch in early 2027, with CES in January being a very likely launch timeline for the latest foldable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The art of making a sandwich has been revered since John Montagu, the fourth Earl of Sandwich, was so engrossed in a game of cards in 1762 he demanded meat between slices of bread to fuel his playing — it was a deeply espresso martini-coded move which saw all of his jealous mates also ask for one.

Over 250 years later, the subtle craft of 'wich is championed once again in an online sandwich-making simulator that threatens to eat into my GTA 6 time.

In a recent development, created by German developer Gregor Weichbrodt with music by Scott Hühnerkrisp, a new sandwich simulator is exactly that. "You make a sandwich. That's all," reads the simulator's about page. Notably, it's not the same as FiftyEight Studios' 2026 game Sandwich Simulator or Sandwich Squad's 2024 Sandwich Sim.

Each sandwich gets a serial number and a permalink, so you can revisit your creation later for reasons I can't quite conjure here beyond lunch inspo. To date, 42,375 unique sandwiches have been made on the simulator since it released in Oct. 2026. For example, my tower of power sandwich will probably live on the internet after I shuffle off this mortal coil.

But there's more going on here, with the developer promising "realistic cucumber behavior" (if you put a slice too far on the edge it'll fall off) and "soft body physics" (slices of cheese, salmon, or ham will drape themselves over what's already on the sandwich).

Recent findings suggest that to make a sandwich, all you need to do is add toppings from the array provided in the bottom menu. To add spreads, you tap the pot and a virtual knife will appear; holding your mouse down will drag that butter across the bread. For other toppings like cheese, radishes, crisps, eggs, tomatoes, and whatnot, you just drag your pick from the menu onto your bread.

If you want to get rid of anything, because you've realised you hate radish (you monster), you can just drag it onto the board. And once you're happy with your creation, you can tap the photo button to save it and generate your permalink — a page which gives you a delightful description of all the ingredients. You can also see every sandwich that has ever been created on the game.

In a recent development, yes, this might be the era of GTA 6, but between missions I'll be making salad sandwiches and drawing my own aquarium. Bit of balance, right?

In a recent development, folding phones are entering a new chapter and, if you’re looking to try one for the first time, you might not know exactly where to start. In this guide, we’ll take a look at some of the most important questions to answer when buying a foldable, and dissect how Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Galaxy Z Flip 8 fit the bill to figure out which is the best for you, especially if you’re interested in one this holiday season.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

In a recent development, samsung has three foldables in its lineup this year, two of which are pretty familiar. The Galaxy Z Flip 8 continues the lineup of clamshell-style foldables, offering a form factor similar to that of a classic flip phone. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, meanwhile, is designed to be a normal smartphone on the outside, hiding a tablet within. Finally, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the new kid on the block, offering a compact outer display that opens up to a media-friendly, wider inner panel.

Each one serves a different need, but they all share similar performance and core specs. Here’s a quick rundown of the key details on each device:.

Industry observers note that starting with the displays, the book-style Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra both provide outer displays that are fully usable as standard smartphones, while the inner display is useful for multitasking, media, or just getting more space for reading a website or e-book. Samsung’s top-tier specs deliver performance for everything you’d need, with Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy powering everything from demanding games or media-editing apps to day-to-day use.

In a recent development, with each Samsung foldable, you’re getting a fully capable smartphone, but finding the one that’s best for you is a matter of picking your most key priorities. Cameras, battery life, content consumption, and size are some of the most important points to consider, so let’s take a look one-by-one.

When it comes to cameras, foldables have a tough time. There’s only so much physical space to fit the camera sensors and, with cameras, having more space generally results in a battery overall camera.

That said, the best camera on a Samsung foldable is undoubtedly on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

In a recent development, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a 200MP main camera that’s similar to the Galaxy S26 Ultra, while it also packs a 50MP ultrawide and something neither of the others offer, a telephoto lens. The 10MP telephoto shooter captures faraway subjects at 3x optical zoom, meaning you’re not giving up on quality when you zoom in. Two 10MP cameras can be found on the displays, with neither sacrificing quality for an under-display look.

Runner-up here is the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which offers a pair of 50MP cameras for wide and ultrawide shots. You can get 2x optical-quality zoom out of the main sensor to still get a good zoom shot, while the main camera still offers good quality and Samsung’s best camera features including 2x optical-quality zoom and the subject-tracking My FanCam.

It has been revealed that the Galaxy Z Flip 8 may not have the best camera hardware, but what it lacks in hardware it makes up for in flexibility. This is definitely the best form factor of the bunch for using the foldable design as a tripod for capturing clips. All three devices also use their foldable nature to let you capture full-quality selfies using the rear cameras, which always have better quality than the 10MP dedicated front-facing cameras.

Here’s where specs on paper can tell a different story compared to real life.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra may offer the biggest battery of the bunch at 5,000 mAh, but its battery life is on par with the smaller Galaxy Z Fold 8. Both foldables are designed to last you through a full day, though sticking to the outer display only on the Fold 8 Ultra may bring you slightly better battery life overall.

In a recent development, in either case, you’re also getting 45W fast charging over USB-C, granting you speedy recharging if your device happens to get low through the course of a busy day. These are also “Qi2 Ready,” meaning you can use magnetic wireless chargers if you use a compatible magnetic case.

One of the most important things you’ll want to ask yourself when buying a foldable phone is why you want to opt for a foldable in the first place, and each of these devices gives a different answer.

According to recent reports, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is a productivity powerhouse, delivering more space on its inner display for you to get work done through the web, apps, and more. You can run up to three apps at once on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s display, as well as floating apps, and more.

It has been revealed that galaxy Z Fold 8 is great for media consumption. The wider aspect ratio is perfect for watching videos, playing games, reading books, and more, all while still giving you plenty of space for productivity just like the Ultra.

Sources indicate that galaxy Z Flip 8, meanwhile, is all about giving you a more compact device. The outer display lets you quickly reply to messages or keep up with directions, while you can unfold it to do everything you want to on a normal phone. Close it up to more easily stow it away in your pocket or your bag.

If you are moving into a new Galaxy foldable, the good news is that you don’t have to start from scratch. Thanks to Samsung’s Smart Switch app, you can easily transfer supported content including pictures, contacts, messages, and more from an older Galaxy phone, another Android phone, or even an iPhone over to a Galaxy foldable. Apps, messages, photos, and more can all make the move wirelessly, without the need of a cable.

You can get the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra, and Flip 8 from your favorite carriers and retailers, but Best Buy is one of the best places to score a great deal with solid trade-in values and deep discounts around Black Friday and throughout the holiday season.

UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….
  • According to recent reports, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue ….

According to recent reports, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

According to recent reports, the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

In 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

This would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve said many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

It would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the manufacturer found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple revealed it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

“Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to new users and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have stated many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

At this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

In a recent development, the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

According to recent reports, the UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal said. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it debuted – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

This ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

If you spot a solid discount on a Pokémon TCG pack, box, or collection you haven’t seen before (like a 30th Celebration ETB, Delta Reign Booster Bundle, etc.), it’s worth buying now rather than waiting for Black Friday.

It has been revealed that when you see a particular price drop, that deal is more likely specific to one or several sellers than to the industry market price across all sellers — depending on their own stock allocations. When that stock is gone, it’s uncertain whether those sellers will have any more units coming in, or even at the same lower price point.

Although more Pokémon cards are being printed than ever in 2026, the Pokémon TCG still has the same matter that sees any readily available selection of packs, or boxes of packs, being sold for above MSRP: There is nowhere near enough supply to meet the demand.

As a result, prices for readily available cards are dictated by market price: estimated by factors like pull rates, the most valuable cards in an expansion, how many print runs an expansion has had, and their overall contribution to the meta.

Day-to-day deals vary between standard Pokémon TCG retailers like Amazon, Walmart, and Target — but the best Black Friday deals are likely to be from third-party sellers operating through those storefronts. There are a lot of sellers competing for sales with one another to offload their stock, and Black Friday is still the ideal season to undercut other Pokémon TCG merchants. Keep checking this guide and store listings each day for the best newly revealed deals.

Apparently, Samsung plans new Galaxy Watch software updates next year as well as “enhancement of healthcare features.” The Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker is also expected in 2027, with Dealabs reporting that the tracker will be priced at €79.90 in Europe, a slight price hike over the previous release.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what consumers need to know.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

Sources indicate that “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

Recent findings suggest that on the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly states it has no plans for a native Mac app.

According to recent reports, you can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft intends to offer an export option before the apps retire.

According to recent reports, planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the company.

Sources indicate that the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the company behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

It has been revealed that microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

Does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Revision: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

In a recent development, “We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team looks. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Fitbit Air is a simple screenless fitness tracker, but it can do a bit more, and now someone has built an app that lets the Air buzz your wrist when phone notifications come through.

The era of vibe-coding has been very swiftly bringing ideas to reality, and these new Fitbit Air notification apps are a great example.

Sources indicate that “Air Relay” is the result of a developer managing to reverse-engineer a way to control haptics on the Fitbit Air via Bluetooth without affecting Google Health sync. “Cuff” uses the same method while also showing health stats if you don’t want to use Google Health.

According to recent reports, the idea here is pretty simple. You can have apps on your phone ping your Fitbit Air as you choose. “Air Relay” lets you pick select apps and even change the vibration pattern or strength based on the app. You can set “Quiet hours” to prevent notifications while you’re sleeping, and there’s a WhatsApp-specific setting that lets you only get notifications from specific groups or people. A “Find My Air” setting uses Bluetooth strength you help you track down a lost tracker.

While a big part of the appeal of Fitbit Air is its screenless, disconnected nature, having the option to set up alerts for crucial apps or contacts is certainly a useful option.

“Air Relay” is free on Google Play, and Fitbit Air is available for $99.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.
  • That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….
  • Industry observers note that earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….

Industry observers note that earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated concerns coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication matter affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith says it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

AirTag-like trackers for Android and iPhone are everywhere nowadays, but Kodak’s latest SlideTag steps it up with a built-in E-Ink display that can show off your photos, widgets, and more along with being able to track down your items.

Compatible with both the Android Find Hub and Apple Find My networks, the Kodak SlideTag is a tracker inspired by the golden era of Kodak photography. The tracker is built by Reto, the same company that built the Kodak Chamera keychain digital camera.

According to recent reports, slideTag’s premise is relatively simple. You get a tracker with an E-Ink display and a frame in one of eight styles inspired by classic 35mm slides. Those styles are sold in a blind box format, meaning you don’t know what you’re getting until you open the box (unless you buy the full set). There’s also a ninth style that only shows up in one out of every 64 boxes.

The E-Ink display can show six-color versions of your photos, or it can display things like lists, calendars, and more. There’s enough storage on the tracker for a 12-photo slideshow, synced through the Kodak Memory Link app on Android and iOS.

Industry observers note that connect instantly via Bluetooth to the KODAK Memory Link App. From live slideshows and custom QR codes to countdowns and dual-network tracking with Apple Find My and Google’s Find Hub, the KODAK SlideTag seamlessly integrates retro aesthetics into your everyday carry.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most dramatic shifts in the AI landscape is the emergence of intelligent agents that can use iPhone and Mac apps in order to carry out tasks on our behalf.

It has been revealed that we can already use third-party chatbots in this way, and we know Apple is working hard to turn Siri AI into an agent. However, before the firm even gets the chance, banks are already blocking them, and this may be just the start ….

According to recent reports, the science fiction promise of AI has always been to be able to tell a computer what we want done and have the task carried out for us automatically. That’s starting to turn into a reality with the emergence of AI agents.

We’ve already seen Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Muse gain agent capabilities, and Apple is expected to bring these to Siri AI at some point next year.

Sources indicate that earlier this month, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said that the tech giant ultimately wants to go in this direction and may add these abilities next year. CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing Craig Federighi for faster software development, with specific mention of “moving beyond necessary improvements to Siri,” which seems likely to mean agentic capabilities.

Last week also saw a since-deleted Apple job listing detailing looks for autonomous AI agents.

We’ve already seen some of the ways in which this can go wrong, and we recently outlined three significant risks. Wired reports that banks are now responding to these by either blocking AI agents or warning customers that using them can be dangerous.

Wells Fargo even goes as far as using capitals in its latest terms, stating that it will not be responsible for the consequences.

Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK.

We can likely expect similar pushback in sectors like online shopping as companies fear high returns costs and other consequences from mistakes by AI agents.

Personally, I don’t give any AI agents access to any of my banking or other financial services, considering the risks to be too high. I don’t see my position changing any time soon.

What’s your take? Would you trust an AI agent with access to your bank accounts? If not, would Apple launching agentic capabilities for Siri AI change your view? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tool Retrieval is now in preview in the Gemini Interactions API.
  • According to recent reports, we are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help your agents manage large tool libraries more efficiently.
  • We are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tool Retrieval is now in preview in the Gemini Interactions API. Load tool parameter schemas on demand instead of sending your full tool library in every prompt,designed to reduce input tokens and keep tool selection accurate as your agent scales.

Research Scientist, Google DeepMind.

Your browser does not support the audio element.

According to recent reports, we are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help your agents manage large tool libraries more efficiently. By loading parameter schemas only when needed, you reduce latency and input token costs for complex tasks. You can try this feature today in the Interactions API by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading to true in your requests.

We are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently. Instead of loading every tool at once, your agent now keeps a library on standby and only pulls in the specific details it needs for a task. This reduces data usage, speeds up performance, and improves accuracy. You can start using this feature today with our latest Gemini models to build more capable and responsive applications.

Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the Interactions API.

When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.

To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a tool_search tool to your request and set defer_loading: true on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

According to recent reports, inside that single API call, the model searches for issue_refund, the API loads its schema, and the model emits the function_call. All three steps appear in interaction.steps, making it easy to inspect which tools the model considered when debugging tool names or descriptions:.

From here it's normal function calling: your code runs the refund and sends back a function_result.

In a recent development, there's no index to build or host. Gemini runs the search on the server, so the only changes to your code are the new tool and a flag on the tools you want to defer. You can keep your most-used tools loaded up front and defer the long tail.

According to recent reports, tool Retrieval also plays well with prefix caching. Deferred schemas stay out of the start of the prompt, and the schemas the model loads are added later in the conversation, so the cached prefix stays the same from turn to turn.

Sources indicate that tool Retrieval also works with remote MCP servers in the Gemini API. Set defer_loading: true on an mcp_server tool and every tool that server exposes is loaded on demand, so you can connect a large server without listing its tools one by one.

If you maintain your own tool registry, embedding index, or per-user permission filter, declare the tool_search with "execution": "client" and define your search parameters. Client-side retrieval adds one round trip per search, because your app runs the lookup. Tools do not need to be declared upfront, so you can also expose newly introduced tools mid-conversation when a user connects an integration:.

According to recent reports, tool Retrieval has no separate charge. Input and output tokens are billed at the standard rates for the model you call. Turning on tool_search adds a small, fixed block of input tokens, and each schema the model loads is billed as input for the rest of the conversation, the same as a tool declared up front. You save tokens when the schemas you never load outweigh the ones you do, which is the usual case for large libraries. Measure it against your own traffic.

Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including all Gemini 4 models, in the Interactions API.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that nvidia has revealed that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The organization’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It remarked that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

He won’t make that mistake again!

It has been revealed that despite putting the company at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, noted that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones noted: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” stated Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Organization. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

According to recent reports, “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a newly introduced industrial revolution,” stated Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

Sources indicate that as previously unveiled, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The company’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • What gives quantum computers their unique power?
  • Recent findings suggest that until recently, this effect had mostly been shown in small systems of just a few particles.

Today, in newly introduced research published on the cover of Science, Google Quantum AI demonstrated that contextuality — a quantum property scientists believe powers certain quantum algorithms — survives at scale on our quantum processor.

What gives quantum computers their unique power? While entanglement usually gets the spotlight, theory suggests that a deeper quantum property called contextuality may power certain quantum algorithms. In simple terms, contextuality means a system’s properties aren’t fixed in advance; what you measure depends on which other compatible measurements you make alongside it.

Recent findings suggest that until recently, this effect had mostly been shown in small systems of just a few particles. Our paper in Science now demonstrates this at scale on our quantum processor. Using it, our qubits won a well-known coordination game 98.3% of the time, beating the 88.9% classical limit, and outperformed constrained classical strategies in tasks spanning up to 105 qubits.

These tests also serve as a sensitive new method to catch subtle hardware errors, helping pave the way for real-world applications like chemistry and materials science. Read the full Google Research blog post to learn more.
